thread:
Alex (Support): FYI - multiple 503s from hosted inference customers hitting /v1/generate. Started ~2026-03-16T10:10Z, spike at 10:12. Customer attached request id req_acme_7c9f. Gateway shows upstream closed connection.
Nina (Oncall): Copy. Any runner logs or container restarts to share?
Alex (Support): Pasting snippet from hosted-runner-42 logs around 10:11:
```
[10:11:22] runner: processing request req_acme_7c9f
[10:11:23] runtime ERR: cudaMemcpy failed: out of memory
[10:11:23] runtime FATAL: Segmentation fault (core dumped)
[kubelet] container runtime: killing container, exit code 139
[kubelet] restarting container hosted-runner-42 (restartCount=3)
[10:11:40] gateway WARN: upstream closed connection, returning 503
```
Alex (Support): Customer says they sent ~120k token context and had kv_prefetch=true in their client.
Kevin (Eng Runtime): That stack looks like an OOM followed by a segfault in the kvcache/prefetch path. We shipped runtime 2.3.1 last week that changed prefetch alignment; could be exposing a boundary condition for >64k contexts.
Priya (ML): Confirmed: model "large-model-v2" prefetcher will allocate for full prefix when PREFETCH=1. With extremely long contexts memory spikes. We had no upper clamp configured for hosted pools.
Nina (Oncall): Immediate mitigation: I'm going to cordon host-gpu-07 and scale the pool down to drain that host. Also flipping routing so requests with context >50k go to fallback small-model-v1. Applying now.
Alex (Support): Notifying impacted customers with temporary workaround: set max_context to 50k or use streaming chunking. Support note added.
ops-bot: AUTO: scaled hosted-pool-03 desired=12->20 (burst scale) to absorb traffic at 10:15Z
Kevin (Eng Runtime): Can reproduce locally. Repro steps: run loadgen with PREFETCH=1, CONTEXT_TOKENS=120000, model=large-model-v2, qps=10. Example curl:
```
PREFETCH=1 CONTEXT=120000 ./tools/loadgen --model large-model-v2 --qps 10 --inject-long-prefix
```
We see OOM then segfault in ~30s.
Priya (ML): Short-term patch: limit prefetch window to 64k in runtime 2.3.2-rc1. I'll open a PR with a guard and a telemetry counter for prefetch bytes.
Kevin (Eng Runtime): Rolling deploy of runtime 2.3.2-rc1 to hosted-pool-03 will be scheduled after canary on 3 nodes. Until then we should drop PREFETCH flag at the gateway for hosted customers by default (override header X-Enable-Prefetch=false).
Nina (Oncall): Done: gateway override applied at 10:20Z for hosted-pool-03. Monitoring for error rate. Alert threshold set to 5% 503 for 5m.
Alex (Support): Customer confirmed error rate dropped after we disabled prefetch and routed large contexts to fallback. They remain concerned about requests that legitimately need >64k; added to escalation for enterprise private deployment.
Priya (ML): Follow-ups: add prefetch safe-limit doc, add config to allow customers to opt-in with explicit quota, and add regression test for long-context prefetch.
Kevin (Eng Runtime): I'll attach the core dump analysis to the postmortem. Initial look suggests a use-after-free in prefetch buffer when retry path triggers concurrent free + mmap.
Nina (Oncall): Monitoring window: 2 hours. If stable, we'll peel back temporary routing changes and proceed with canary 2.3.2 next week. Also filing incident ticket for PM/SE outreach.
Alex (Support): Notes for handoff: customer impacted: Acme AI (account-acme-019), request ids and timestamps included in the ticket. Support to follow up with mitigation guide.
Priya (ML): PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/472 (prefetch clamp + telemetry) - marked high priority.
Kevin (Eng Runtime): +1. After canary success we'll perform rolling update and collect crash histogram.
Alex (Support): Thanks all. I'll update the customer and mark this thread for postmortem. :thumbsup:
